claims.text: The baseline FeCoNiTi alloy is equiatomic, corresponding to approximately 25 at.% each of Fe, Co, Ni, and Ti.
Equiatomic or near-equiatomic FeCoNiTi is a high-entropy alloy.
The baseline FeCoNiTi alloy exhibits standard magnetocaloric behavior.
Deviating from equiatomic FeCoNiTi stoichiometry will enhance the magnetocaloric response near the magnetic phase transition.
Changing FeCoNiTi composition adjusts the balance between magnetic and non-magnetic elements.
The proposed intervention is to systematically increase or decrease the concentrations of selected magnetic elements in FeCoNiTi.
The proposed experiments will survey a broad compositional range under controlled temperatures and applied magnetic fields.
Compositional modification of FeCoNiTi causes lattice distortion.
Composition-induced lattice distortion alters the magnetic-domain structure.
Composition-induced lattice distortion changes the phase fractions.
Adjusting the concentrations of magnetic elements changes magnetic interaction strengths.
Adjusting the concentrations of magnetic elements shifts the Curie temperature.
Changes in magnetic interaction strengths and Curie temperature increase the magnetic entropy change during magnetization and demagnetization.
Optimized compositions will exhibit a larger magnetic entropy change than baseline equiatomic FeCoNiTi.
Optimized compositions will exhibit a larger adiabatic temperature change near the phase transition than baseline equiatomic FeCoNiTi.
The baseline equiatomic FeCoNiTi alloy is prepared by arc melting followed by rapid quenching.
Magnetocaloric improvement is expected only over the composition range that preserves a high-entropy single-phase structure.
Excessive deviation from the baseline FeCoNiTi composition may cause deleterious phase separation.
